pitches.logline: Bertha Benz, Karl Benz's wife, takes his unsold Patent-Motorwagen with their two sons without telling him, but the car keeps failing on the way to Pforzheim.
pitches.hook: Frame 0: the Motorwagen rolling down the poplar road, then it coughs and stops dead mid-road and Bertha rises from the bench; sound real-sputter

pitches.logline: Bertha Benz runs out of fuel far from home in her husband's car, and the only place that sells it is a pharmacy, which is how Wiesloch's pharmacy came to be called the world's first filling station.
pitches.hook: Frame 0: the hero cranks the Motorwagen in a small town street and it will not start; sound real-no-start

pitches.logline: Karl Benz's Motorwagen sells to nobody, so his wife Bertha quietly drives it about 106 km with their sons, keeping it alive on the way, and proves to the world it works.
pitches.hook: Frame 0: a downhill, the wooden brakes screech and slip, mother and two boys lean back; sound real-brake-squeal

treatment.logline: Bertha Benz, Karl Benz's wife, takes his Patent-Motorwagen without asking him and drives it from Mannheim to Pforzheim, and on the way the car keeps failing.
treatment.hero: Bertha Benz: the real portrait and her silhouette in a long dress by the one Motorwagen, the same all film
treatment.obstacle: A car nobody has driven that far: fuel sold only in pharmacies, a blocked fuel line, a wire to insulate, wooden brakes wearing out

hook.event: Mid-road on the poplar road the Motorwagen coughs, jolts and dies, the smoke thins out and Bertha rises on the bench

act1: It needs fuel: she stops at the pharmacy in Wiesloch (the town's stone and a shop front, then the real pharmacy photo)
Worse: the fuel line blocks, she crouches at the car and clears it with her hat pin
Worse still: a wire needs insulating and her garter goes round it
Worst: the wooden brakes wear out on a downhill and a cobbler fits leather to them
treatment.turn: The twist card on the hold: the man invented it, the woman took it on the road (one punch word, her name), 0.7 s

reveal.what: The twist: the man invented the car, the woman proved it runs; then the world gets to know it and the buyers come

treatment.payoff: The same Bertha by the same car at the Pforzheim stone in the low sun, her boys beside her: it died, yet she got there, and the world got to know Benz's car
treatment.signature: A poplar road in late light, the three-wheeled Motorwagen in crisp silhouette; each town's roadside stone slides in and stops by the wheel (Mannheim, Wiesloch, Pforzheim)
